findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
The cooler drawers on the cook-line were observed to have an ambient temperature of 50F. Salmon in the bottom cooler drawer was probed at 50F and beef patties in the top cooler drawer were probed at 49F. According to the PIC, the temperature of the cooler drawers were last checked at 12pm and were observed to be at 39F. The TCS food items in this cooler were placed under Time as Control. It was discussed to use or discard the items by 4pm. The PIC stated that they will cook all of the food items before 4pm. 

The front preparation cooler in the kitchen was observed to have an ambient temperature of 52F. A salad dressing in the top of the preparation cooler was probed at 54F and bread was probed in the bottom of the preparation cooler at 58F. According to the PIC, the temperature of the cooler was last checked at 12pm and was at 37F. The TCS food items in the cooler were placed under Time as Control. It was discussed to use or discard the items in this cooler by 4pm. 

Ensure that TCS foods are cold held at 41F and below.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no Norovirus illness policy available. Provided copy for facility. Bleach is available to perform procedure. Ensure staff is aware of policy. COS.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee was observed improperly washing hands.  Employee did not use barrier to turn off water. Ensure proper procedure is used when washing hands.  Wash for 20 seconds, rinse, dry with paper towel, then turn off water using barrier.

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Soda nozzles at the server stations were observed to have a build-up of mold.  If not cleaned and sanitized nightly, soda nozzles may accumulate a build-up of mold and debris.  Ensure soda nozzles are cleaned and sanitized regularly to prevent contamination. The bar soda nozzle holder outside was observed to have mold build up. Inspector showed employee. Employee began to wash, rinse, sanitize the soda nozzle holder. Ensure staff is aware to clean both the soda nozzles themselves and the soda nozzle holders.

Observed the back ice machine (very back of restaurant) to have heavy accumulation of mold along the interior baffle. See attached photo page. Ensure staff is aware to wash, rinse, sanitize the ice machines regularly in order to prevent mold accumulation.

Shelving in dish area holding clean dishes and equipment were observed to contain a build-up of dust and food debris.  Shelving is in need of deep cleaning, and suggested to PIC laying a barrier on racks to help prevent the dust build-up from contaminating clean food contact surfaces.  Ensure shelving is cleaned regularly to prevent dust build-up and contamination of food contact surfaces.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the outside bar area dish machine to not being sanitizing correctly. Machine utilizes bleach per the outside of the machine and the sanitizer bottle. It should be at least 50 ppm. Sanitizer was changed and the machine was run 3-4x times. No bleach was dispensing from the dish machine. Employee in this area is putting a sign not to use the dish machine until repaired. Plastic utensils are going to be used in this area until the situation is fixed with the dish machine. Inspector will follow-up on 9/21/22.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Raw beef stored in drawer coolers under the grill were observed to be 62F (probed).  PIC stated beef was put there at 11:00.  Kitchen employee was asked to move the beef into the walk-in cooler to cool.  Drawers are not keeping temperature and should not be used for cold holding.  Ensure beef and other raw meats are not kept in drawer cooler to prevent contamination.

Observed the prep cooler directly across from the grill to be out of temperature. The top of this prep cooler has historically been utilized on a time control with items every 4 hours being changed per PIC. The bottom of this prep cooler was ~57F. All food items were moved to the reach-in cooler near the dish machine area. PIC stated items were prepped that morning. The entire prep cooler is not functioning correctly. Time controlling food items (top prep cooler behavior) is a temporary solution and fix. It is not intended for everyday use. This prep cooler either needs to be entirely replaced and/or properly fixed so the entire unit is functioning (holding below 41F). 

A temperature log was provided during this inspection so staff can start logging daily am/pm temps of ALL cold holding units. Ensure copies are made and posted on all cold holding units and staff begins logging process. The amount of coolers that are not working properly at the facility shows a lack of oversight from management in temperature control at the facility. 

Inspector will follow-up on 9/21/22 due to this inspection being on a late Friday before a weekend regarding drawer coolers, prep cooler, and temperature log use on all cold holding units. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
-Prep cooler on far right of the kitchen prep line is out of service.  PIC stated cooler has not worked for about 6 years.  They are currently using a Time as Control procedure for prep items and replacing food every 4 hours, although they do not have a Time as Control agreement with SCDPH.  Prep cooler is in need of being fixed, replaced or removed.  Ensure a Time as Control agreement is signed and a log is kept recording times of food being put in cooler and being replaced.  A temperature log and Time as Control agreement is discussed with PIC.

-Bar cooler was observed to have water pooled at the bottom of the cooler.  Bartender stated someone was notified and coming out to fix the cooler.  Ensure cooler is repaired to prevent leak from occurring.  

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed a large amount of frozen ponding water in one of the walk-in freezers. The ice was significant and the walk-in freezer should not be routinely kept this way. Ensure repairs and/or ensure staff is aware to secure the door (if this is causing the issue). Discussed with PIC. Ensure situation is rectified before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Ceiling and vents were observed to have an accumulation of dust and grease debris.  PIC stated they were in the process of cleaning the ceiling and vents.  Some ceiling tiles were observed to have been cleaned recently.  Ensure the remainder of the ceiling and vents are cleaned and free of dust and debris to prevent contamination of food.

Other areas in need of wash, rinse, and sanitizing (non-food contact surfaces):
1. Interior fryer doors were heavily soiled with grease and food debris. Ensure fryers are routinely cleaned to prevent debris and hinder pest issues.
2. Small fan above the prep line was soiled with dust.
3. Walk-in cooler fans had accumulation of dust (2x).
4. Ledge around the entire dish machine area was dusty.
5. Floor of walk-in freezer was soiled with food spillage.

Ensure the above areas are addressed and cleaned. Ensure staff maintains routine cleaning of facility as needed to prevent dirt, debris, dust, etc.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed a hole in the wall behind the ovens that was singed from heat. Area has not been repaired. Ensure repairs to make smooth and easily cleanable. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/23/22.

Observed the following areas in need of repairs:
1. Paint on wall near the hand sink in the kitchen is chipped and pealing. Ensure all paint on the kitchen walls is smooth and repaint any additional areas as needed.
2. Hand sink at kitchen has old caulking - re-caulk the hand sink (also the interior creases in the hand sink, as well as the sink to the wall).
3. Thawing sink needs caulked to the wall (no caulk).
4. The entire dish machine area needs caulked to the wall. No caulk.
5. Mop sink needs caulking - re-caulk as needed.

Discussed with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection. Facility should be smooth, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent regarding materials of walls, ceilings, and floors.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed no allergen training certification for any CFPM at the facility. Provide copies for the public health folder. Ensure all certified food protection manager’s have allergen training. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT, and utensil is washed, rinsed, and sanitized at least every 4 hours. 

Observed ice scoop in server station to have handle in direct contact with ice. Inspector removed scoop and placed on soda machine. See that servers are placing scoops in a designated container and not in ice.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. 

Both prep coolers on the line are observed to have a leak, causing water to pool in the bottom. Currently, facility is using rags to soak up excess water and changes them frequently. See that the prep coolers are repaired by a technician or replaced to prevent leak from occurring. Cease use of rags in cooler as this risks breeding pathogens and causes a cross contamination risk. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-501.18: The wash, rinse, and SANITIZE solutions shall be maintained clean. 

At the 3-compartment sink in the bar, observed the sink to be set up in the following order: wash, sanitize, rinse (with the blue quaternary ammonium solution in the center basin). Discussed with bartender and front of house manager. See that the sink is always set up in the following order: wash, rinse, sanitize to ensure the process of ware washing occurs according to code. The sink may either go right to left or left to right, that does not matter as long as wash, rinse, sanitize is in order.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Behind the ovens in the kitchen, there is a hole in the wall and the wall is singed from heat. This area is no longer smooth and easily cleanable in this condition. Discussed with PIC, see that the wall is repaired and consider adding a layer of sheet metal to the wall to protect it from heat.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

Observed staff member filling a frying pan with water using the handwashing sink. Discussed with PIC and staff in kitchen. See that staff use other sinks for filling/food prep, leave handwashing sinks for handwashing only.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT, and utensil is washed, rinsed, and sanitized at least every 4 hours. 

Observed two knives stored between prep coolers and prep tables in the cooking area. Cease practice of storing utensils between equipment crevices as these areas are not regularly cleaned and pose a contamination risk to prepared foods. Store knives on top of prep surfaces. Wash, rinse, and sanitize utensils as needed or at least every 4 hours. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm).

Bar dish machine is not sanitizing. After 2 washes and a priming of the sanitizer lines, the test strip still reads at 0ppm. findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.
(B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

Upon arrival, inspector observed a pitcher in the handsink, blocking the sink and indicating use other than handwashing. Ensure handwashing sink is free and accessible at all times and no filling, dumping, or storing of any items at any time. Education provided.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Cole Slaw probed at 50 degrees, potato salad probed at 50 degrees. External thermometer indicated 32.5 degrees while internal was reading 50. Prep cook stated he just completed prepping and storing the individually-portioned slaws and potato salad in cooler. 
Items not just prepped, leftover from previous night (cheesecake and sheet cake for example) probed at 43 degrees. 
Time as control policy created for all food items stored in this fridge. It is apparent that in times of intense activity/prep the food items have trouble maintain proper cold holding temperatures. All items must be used or discarded within 4 hours. Facility will only place food items used within the timeframes outlined in policy (11-2,2-6,6-10). All bulk storage of food items or overnight storages must occur in other equipment in kitchen per the policy. 
In the long run, facility is looking to replace cooler completely due to repetitive issues with keeping temperature. 
No additional follow up regarding this cooler required at this time.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation

750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.
750-160bGloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interuption in operations.

750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed wiping cloths laying around the kitchen and dish room area. Store all wiping cloths in a properly sanitized bucket when not in use or in it's designated area for soiled cloths.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed the soda nozzles in the waitress area to be soiled with what appears to be mold. Wash, rinse, and sanitize the soda nozzles in the waitress area. The soda nozzles were replaced during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained

Observed the floors in the kitchen and dish area to be soiled. Clean the floors in the kitchen and dish area.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.comment: Observed a jacket stored in the dry storage room. Store all employee belongings in a designated locker area away from food areas. 750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: See 7/2/18 inspection.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed deli meats and coleslaw in the prep cooler on the side of the kitchen nearest the dish room to be probed with a recently calibrated digital thermometer at internal temperatures of 63-86F and 60F respectively. Deli meats were stacked well above the fill line on the containers and it was discussed that these containers should not be filled past those lines, and stocked more often. Deli meats out of temperature were discarded during the inspection. Coleslaw was reported to have been stocked around 4 pm and may be used until 8 pm, then this cooler should be turned over. A thermometer left in the bottom of this prep cooler read 48F but is also opened repeatedly (and one of the door hinges is broken).
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed scrambled eggs and mashed potatoes in the hot box next to the hand sink in the kitchen to be probed at internal temperatures of 118F and 130F respectively. Hot box temperature was adjusted. Hot foods must be held at 135F or above at all times.
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed pasta (macaroni) salad and corned beef cooling in the walk in cooler to be probed at internal temperatures of 60-64F and 70F respectively. Pasta salad was reported to have been made by the prep person who left work at 11:45am. Corned beef was reported to have been 165F at 2:30 pm when it was shredded. There were no times as to when the cooling process began on any of these items. When cooling, the time the cooling process begins must be recorded, and items cooled rapidly to 70F within 2 hours and then to 41F or below within an additional 4 hours (as long as it was 70F within 2 hours). Two tubs of pasta salad and two pans of corned beef were voluntarily discarded during the inspection.
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:

750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

750-160 Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact.

750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.

750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

CORRECTED> Observed the hand sink in the kitchen to be blocked by trash can. Trash can was moved to correct the violatioin and make hand sink accessible.
750-1120(b) Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: REPEAT 1x> 1) Mop sink is pulling away from wall. Recaulk sink to wall. REPEAT 1x> 2) Wall at mop sink is in disrepair. Repair wall to make for a smooth and easily cleanable surface. REPEAT 1x> 3) hole in wall in mopsink room left of door upon entering. Fill hole and paint to make smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Multiple items in black mini refrigerator were out of temperature. Nine bottles of dressing and a container of pickles were probed and temperatures of 49-59F were recorded. Items were discarded.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed potentially hazardous foods being held in hot water bath on stove to be below 135F. Surface temperatures were 110F-120F. Internal temperature of queso was at 124F, while chicken gravy, mushroom gravy, vodka sauce, and vegetables and internal temperatures of 130F-133F. Water in hot bath had evaporated down, and burners were not on at a high setting upon arrival of inspectors. Kitchen Manager had cook discard all products and reheat all fresh products. Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135F/above. Maintain adequate hot water baths and keep burners at a high enough setting to help keep foods at proper temperature.
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed raw bacon to be stored above ready-to-eat foods in stainless refrigerator. Items were rearranged to proper order.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Improper glove use was noted during the inspection. One employee was observed wiping finger tips of gloved hands on a cloth towel. Another employee was observed going in and out of the building to get containers of food from the walkin cooler and transfer foods to clean equipment wearing gloves. Proper glove use was discussed at length. Both employees washed their hands and changed gloves. Common towels must never be used to wipe hands for any reason.
750-160b Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.
750-1120e Common towels are prohibited.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be in disrepair: 1) ice accumulation in black mini-refrigerator/freezer. 2) ice accumulation in walk in freezer. Defrost equipment to remove ice. 3) Spray sink table pulling away from wall. Move back to wall and recaulk to make easily cleanable.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed QUAT concentration at bar 3-pan sink to be 100 ppm. Tablets were added and retested to be 200 ppm.
750-820d Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Sanitizer bucket tested >200 ppm CL. Bucket was corrected to 200 ppm QUAT.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed bus tubs of wrapped silverware on the floor under metal cabinet at wait station. Store cleaned/sanitized utensils and equipment up off the ground at least 6 inches.
750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the following floors to be soiled or in disrepair: 1) soiled floor below cook line/prep line. 2) soiled floor in dry storage.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following walls to be soiled or in disrepair: 1) holes in wall to left of hand sink in kitchen. Fill in holes to make smooth and easily cleanable. 2) Mop sink needs recaulked to wall. 3) Wall at mop sink in disrepair. Replace dry wall or paint to make smooth and easily cleanable. 4) hole in wall in mopsink room left of door upon entering. Fill hole and paint to make smooth and easily cleanable.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
